faq_changes.question: What is the difference between adjustable and fixed closet shelving?

before.q: What is the difference between adjustable and fixed closet shelving?
a: Adjustable shelving hangs from a wall mounted rail so shelves, rods and accessories can be moved at any time, while fixed shelving fastens directly to the wall and stays in one configuration. Adjustable suits closets whose contents change, such as a child's room, a shared closet, or a household that shifts things seasonally. Fixed gives a cleaner built in look and suits a settled layout.
Organized Living's adjustable lines are freedomRail and freedomRail EDGE. VUE, Select and Classica are fixed.

after.q: What is the difference between adjustable and fixed closet shelving?
a: Adjustable storage allows shelves, rods and compatible accessories to be repositioned after the mounting system is installed. Fixed storage follows the specified mounting positions and supports. The distinction concerns the mounting system; the finish and shelf surface are separate choices.

Our freedomRail and freedomRail EDGE collections provide adjustable rail storage. VUE and fixed ventilated wire use fixed supports. Select and Classica provide built-in cabinetry, with some shelf adjustment available in Select configurations.

after.q: What is the difference between freedomRail and freedomRail EDGE?

faq_changes.question: Is wire shelving or wood shelving better for a closet?

before.q: Is wire shelving or wood shelving better for a closet?
a: Ventilated wire is better where airflow, cost per foot and load capacity matter most, and wood is better where appearance and a solid shelf surface matter more. Wire suits pantries, linen closets, laundry rooms and garages, and it does not trap moisture. Wood suits primary bedroom closets and any space where the closet reads as part of the room's finish.
Organized Living manufactures both. Lifetime and Shelftech are ventilated wire, and VUE is fixed wood shelving.

after.q: Is wire shelving or wood shelving better for a closet?
a: Ventilated wire provides an open shelf surface. Solid laminate provides a continuous surface for folded items and smaller objects, with finishes that coordinate with the room. The stored items, shelf supports, finish and available space determine the appropriate choice.

Our Lifetime and Shelftech collections are fixed ventilated wire systems. VUE is fixed solid thermally fused laminate shelving. Product documents establish load and installation requirements; wire construction alone does not guarantee moisture resistance or a higher capacity.

faq_changes.question: How should I plan a pantry?

before.q: How should I plan a pantry?
a: Plan a pantry by mapping what you store by frequency and height before choosing shelf spacing, so daily items sit at eye level, bulk and seasonal items go high or low, and deep shelves hold bins rather than loose goods. Ventilated wire suits pantries because air moves around packaged food and the shelving carries heavy tinned and bulk goods without sagging.

Reach in pantries usually work best with fixed shelving at graduated spacings. Walk in pantries benefit from adjustable shelving on at least one wall, so the spacing can change as what you buy changes.

after.q: How should I plan a pantry?

faq_changes.question: Can closets be specified to meet ADA reach ranges?

before.q: Can closets be specified to meet ADA reach ranges?
a: Closet shelves and rods can be specified within ADA reach ranges, which under the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design set unobstructed high reach at 48 inches maximum and unobstructed low reach at 15 inches minimum above the floor. Adjustable systems such as freedomRail make this straightforward, because rod and shelf heights are set at installation rather than fixed at manufacture.

Where a reach is obstructed the standards tighten, allowing an obstruction no more than 34 inches high and 24 inches deep, and reducing high side reach to 46 inches maximum where reach depth exceeds 10 inches. Compliance for a given project rests with the designer of record, who sets the mounting heights.

after.q: Can closets be specified to meet ADA reach ranges?
a: Closet storage can be designed around the applicable accessibility requirements. The ADA Standards identify a 15-inch minimum and 48-inch maximum for unobstructed adult reach. Forward and side reaches over obstructions have different limits, so the approach and obstruction must be evaluated separately.
The project designer must assess reach, clear floor space, approach and mounting heights together. An adjustable product does not by itself establish a compliant installation.

faq_changes.question: What applies on federally funded projects?

before.q: What applies on federally funded projects?
a: Federally funded infrastructure projects are subject to the Build America, Buy America Act, which requires the iron and steel, manufactured products and construction materials used in the project to be produced in the United States. The Act applies to projects funded after 14 May 2022, and awards receiving less than $250,000 in federal assistance are generally exempt, though some agencies set higher thresholds. For iron and steel, all production stages from initial melting through coating must occur in the United States.

Organized Living products are made in the USA, with every product line manufactured at the company's Bloomington, Indiana facility. Contact the sales team for the domestic content documentation your project requires, since Build America, Buy America compliance is evidenced per project rather than held as a standing certification.

after.q: What applies on federally funded projects?
a: Covered federally assisted infrastructure projects may have domestic-content requirements under Build America, Buy America. Applicability, product classification and any waiver depend on the funding agency, award and current requirements; there is no single exemption threshold suitable for every project.

Request documentation for the specified products from our sales team and have the project team confirm the applicable procurement requirements. A general manufacturing-origin statement is not a project compliance certification.
